title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #5

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the difference between hearing and listening? (1 mark)
   A. Hearing needs effort but listening does not
   B. They are exactly the same
   C. Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
   D. Hearing is only for adults

2. What is a good first step when reading for information? (1 mark)
   A. Copy the title
   B. Close the book
   C. Ask what you want to find out
   D. Guess the ending

3. Which is a clue that a noun is plural? (1 mark)
   A. A number word such as three before it
   B. A capital letter
   C. A full stop
   D. The word the

4. Which is a good way to practise the shape of a letter? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it
   B. Ignore it
   C. Trace it in the air with your finger
   D. Rub it out

5. What does an oral text mean? (1 mark)
   A. A text written on a wall
   B. A text drawn on paper
   C. A text that is spoken
   D. A text printed only

6. In Simon says, when should you obey an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Always
   C. Only if you like it
   D. Only when it begins with Simon says

7. Which word in Bring the clothes inside is the verb? (1 mark)
   A. Bring
   B. clothes
   C. the
   D. inside

8. Why is reading fluently important? (1 mark)
   A. It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   B. It hides mistakes
   C. It ends the lesson early
   D. It makes the book smaller

9. Where should commas go in: We planted maize beans peas and kale? (1 mark)
   A. After planted
   B. After We
   C. After maize and beans
   D. After kale

10. Which sentence has the punctuation of a list correct? (1 mark)
   A. We wore, hats scarves and coats.
   B. We wore hats scarves, and coats
   C. We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   D. We wore hats scarves and coats.

11. Which of these must always begin with a capital letter in English? (1 mark)
   A. The names of colours
   B. The names of weather
   C. The names of foods
   D. The names of people

12. Why should you look back at the dialogue when answering questions? (1 mark)
   A. To find accurate answers
   B. To copy a friend
   C. To hide the page
   D. To waste time

13. What is a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. A group of animals
   B. A type of word
   C. A kind of poem
   D. The order in which things happen

14. What can wall charts of similes and metaphors help with? (1 mark)
   A. Running
   B. Cooking
   C. Gallery walks and learning from each other
   D. Sleeping

15. In the metaphor Time is money, what is the meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Time is made of paper
   B. Clocks are coins
   C. Time is valuable and should not be wasted
   D. Money is a clock

16. What does Honesty is the best policy teach? (1 mark)
   A. Telling the truth is the wisest choice
   B. Only rich people are honest
   C. Lying is fine
   D. Truth is unimportant

17. Why do many readers read silently? (1 mark)
   A. Books cannot be read aloud
   B. It is boring
   C. It is illegal to read aloud
   D. It is fast and does not disturb others

18. Why do we explain a proverb in our own words? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To change it forever
   C. To make it longer
   D. To show we understand the lesson

19. What does a peer review checklist help with? (1 mark)
   A. Checking a partner's story kindly
   B. Cleaning the room
   C. Stealing ideas
   D. Ending the lesson

20. What is an imaginative composition? (1 mark)
   A. A weather forecast
   B. A story made from the imagination
   C. A list of prices
   D. A news report

21. A saying such as It is raining cats and dogs means (1 mark)
   A. it is raining very heavily
   B. animals are falling
   C. dogs and cats are lost
   D. the weather is cold

22. What does a conjunction do? (1 mark)
   A. Shows a feeling
   B. Describes a colour
   C. Joins words or sentences
   D. Names a thing

23. What should you do with the events of a story you tell? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the beginning
   B. Tell them in the order they happened
   C. Mix them up
   D. Never mention the end

24. What is scanning? (1 mark)
   A. Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   B. Writing a story
   C. Reading for the main idea only
   D. Singing

25. Which word shows a result? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. but
   C. and
   D. so

26. The bag is below the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. on
   C. between
   D. beside

27. What should you do while listening to instructions about where to place objects? (1 mark)
   A. Move immediately
   B. Look away
   C. Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   D. Talk

28. Which pair of words rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. day and play
   B. hen and goat
   C. water and food
   D. cow and shade

29. What should you do while another speaker is talking in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. Leave
   B. Laugh
   C. Talk loudly
   D. Listen without interrupting

30. What are peers? (1 mark)
   A. People of your own age or class
   B. Animals
   C. Only parents
   D. Only teachers

31. Why should you not invent interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. They are learned from speakers of the language
   B. Nobody uses them
   C. It is easy to invent them correctly
   D. Languages have no interjections

32. Which interjection shows sudden understanding? (1 mark)
   A. Oops
   B. Ouch
   C. Yuck
   D. Aha

33. What is the main idea of a passage? (1 mark)
   A. The date
   B. The page number
   C. The last word
   D. What it is mostly about

34. What should you do if you dialled a wrong number? (1 mark)
   A. Shout at them
   B. Call again angrily
   C. Stay silent
   D. Say sorry and end the call politely

35. What does a good form have? (1 mark)
   A. No spaces
   B. No title
   C. Clear title, instructions and enough space
   D. Tiny words only

36. What should you do first before filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Fill any box
   B. Sign
   C. Read all the instructions
   D. Fold it

37. Which of these is an action verb? (1 mark)
   A. the
   B. is
   C. lead
   D. very

38. Does every poem have to rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. Yes, always
   B. Only short poems
   C. No
   D. Only long poems

39. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The ink
   B. The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   C. The page number
   D. The title

40. What should each step in written instructions usually start with? (1 mark)
   A. A number only
   B. A verb
   C. A colour
   D. A name

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain what an interjection is and give two examples. (2 marks)

42. Read: The nurse bandaged the wound gently and the blood stopped. What does wound mean? Give two clues. (3 marks)

43. Write three instructions for what to do when it starts to rain at school. Use first, then and finally. (4 marks)

44. Describe how to mark a line of a poem for reading aloud. (4 marks)

45. What is a verb? Give two examples. (2 marks)

46. Read: Fire can be dangerous. Never play with matches. Ask an adult to light the stove. If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. State the main idea and list three details. (5 marks)

47. Explain the steps of organising a class debate. (4 marks)

48. Describe the steps in writing a story from a picture. (4 marks)

49. Write a four-line dialogue between two friends deciding what to do in their free time. Use two interjections. (4 marks)

50. Explain why you should ask an elder or teacher about writing interjections in your mother tongue, and describe how to collect them. (5 marks)

51. Plan a short oral narrative about a school rule. Say the characters, the events, the ending, and where you will use a simile and a metaphor. (5 marks)

52. Give two adjectives to describe a school bag in an advert. (2 marks)

53. Correct this paragraph: it was a cold morning in nyeri the children wore sweaters scarves and socks (4 marks)

54. Give the meaning of comprehension and say why it matters when we listen. (2 marks)

55. List three steps for explaining a proverb. (3 marks)

56. Find the rhyming words in: Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play. (2 marks)

57. What is a conjunction? Give one example. (2 marks)

58. List three steps for understanding a poem. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
   Hearing happens naturally, but listening is a choice to pay attention.

2. C — Ask what you want to find out
   A question in mind helps you look for the right facts.

3. A — A number word such as three before it
   Number words show how many there are.

4. C — Trace it in the air with your finger
   Tracing helps the hand remember the movement.

5. C — A text that is spoken
   Oral means spoken.

6. D — Only when it begins with Simon says
   The game is about listening carefully.

7. A — Bring
   Bring shows the action.

8. A — It helps listeners understand and enjoy the reading
   Fluent reading helps meaning.

9. C — After maize and beans
   The list is maize, beans, peas and kale.

10. C — We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   A comma follows each item except the last two, which are joined by and.

11. D — The names of people
   Names of people and places begin with capital letters.

12. A — To find accurate answers
   Answers should come from the text.

13. D — The order in which things happen
   Sequence means order.

14. C — Gallery walks and learning from each other
   Charts display the sayings for review.

15. C — Time is valuable and should not be wasted
   The metaphor shows the value of time.

16. A — Telling the truth is the wisest choice
   It praises honesty.

17. D — It is fast and does not disturb others
   Silent reading is quiet and lets you think.

18. D — To show we understand the lesson
   Explaining shows understanding of the meaning.

19. A — Checking a partner's story kindly
   Peer review helps improve writing.

20. B — A story made from the imagination
   Imaginative compositions are made-up stories.

21. A — it is raining very heavily
   It is an expression for heavy rain.

22. C — Joins words or sentences
   Conjunctions are joining words.

23. B — Tell them in the order they happened
   Order helps listeners follow.

24. A — Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   Scanning searches for a detail.

25. D — so
   So shows a result.

26. A — under
   Under means below something.

27. C — Listen to the whole instruction before acting
   Full listening avoids mistakes.

28. A — day and play
   Day and play end in the same sound.

29. D — Listen without interrupting
   Good debaters listen.

30. A — People of your own age or class
   Peers are people like you in age or class.

31. A — They are learned from speakers of the language
   Ask real speakers for correct forms.

32. D — Aha
   Aha shows realising something.

33. D — What it is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

34. D — Say sorry and end the call politely
   Politeness matters.

35. C — Clear title, instructions and enough space
   Clarity makes forms easy to fill.

36. C — Read all the instructions
   Reading first prevents mistakes.

37. C — lead
   Lead shows action.

38. C — No
   Some poems do not rhyme.

39. B — The beat or flow when a poem is read aloud
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds.

40. B — A verb
   Steps begin with action words.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: An interjection is a short word or sound showing sudden feeling, for example Wow and Ouch.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for two examples.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wound is an injury. Clues are the nurse, bandaged and blood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and two marks for clues, awarding one for each up to two.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, go into the classroom. Then close the windows. Finally, wait for the rain to stop.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for using all three signal words.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Underline words to stress, draw a slash where you will pause, read the line using your marks and check that it sounds natural.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: A verb is an action word. Examples: run, close, bring, put.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for two correct examples.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Main idea: Fire is dangerous and needs care. Details: never play with matches, ask an adult to light the stove, stop drop and roll.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the main idea and one mark for each of three details.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a motion, form two teams, plan reasons, take turns to speak for about a minute each, listeners note points, the class votes.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, ask who where and what, plan the characters, setting, problem and ending, write the story in order, and check it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines with speaker names, colons, a clear topic and two suitable interjections.
   Working / marking points: One mark for names and colons, one mark for suitable content, one mark for each interjection.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask because spelling and meanings must be correct and not invented. Listen to speakers, write each interjection with its feeling on a flashcard, check spelling with the teacher and sort by feeling.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the reason and three marks for collecting steps.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any plan with characters, events in order, an ending with a lesson, and one simile and one metaphor, for example a pupil who came late but learned that rules are like a map.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, events, ending, simile and metaphor.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: strong, big, red, light, new (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each adjective.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: It was a cold morning in Nyeri. The children wore sweaters, scarves and socks.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four corrections: capitals at the start, Nyeri, the full stops and the commas.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Comprehension means understanding. It matters because we can then remember and use what we heard.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for why it matters.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say it slowly, picture what it shows, decide the lesson, think of a real situation, explain in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: day and play
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: A conjunction is a joining word, such as and, but or when.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for an example.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read it aloud more than once, find meanings of new words, say the message in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
